A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLM-DAS work, and their text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. The supplied v1 ends after its references despite referring to an appendix; v2 supplies Appendix 6.1–6.20. Newly supplied documentation can be distinguished from explicitly introduced extensions.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original evaluations across 36 datasets, component ablations, cross-detector experiments and synthetic-anomaly visualizations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds sensitivity experiments, controlled anomaly-type evaluations, hardness analysis and multi-weakness synthesis results.

M1.justification: The two-stage synthesis pipeline and normalized score fusion remain intact. Sections 6.16–6.18 add optional hardness-controlled synthesis, a mixture targeting multiple detector weaknesses, and a prompt-based proposal for generating detector-specific auxiliary classifiers. These are localized extensions of the retained framework.

E1.justification: Both versions report the 36-dataset ODDS/ADBench benchmark. Section 6.15 adds four controlled Hepatitis-derived test scenarios containing local, global, dependency and clustered anomalies. This extends the evaluated distributions without introducing a broad new application domain.

E2.justification: The main comparison methods remain those already shown in v1 Figure 3, and Gaussian, random and SMOTE synthesis comparisons are retained. Table 19 newly compares LOF with LOF enhanced by LLM-DAS; v1 evaluated LOF only as a standalone comparator, outside its five source-detector enhancement pairings.

E3.justification: The main normal-data split and AUC metrics remain unchanged. Added studies introduce alternative LLM backbones and classifiers, synthesis ratios from 0.1 to 1.0, controlled anomaly-generation procedures, and Wasserstein-based diagnostic metrics (Sections 6.9, 6.12 and 6.15–6.16). These substantially expand evaluation protocols without establishing that the original benchmark was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds backbone and query sensitivity, synthesis-ratio tests, classifier-choice and score-fusion ablations, anomaly-type alignment analysis, hardness-related failure analysis and multi-weakness synthesis comparisons. These investigate robustness and mechanisms beyond v1's retained component ablations, cross-detector experiment and Thyroid visualization.

E5.justification: Tables 4–5 introduce per-dataset ± quantities absent from v1, but do not define their statistical meaning or specify repetition counts and seeds. The paired one-tailed t-test and Table 1 p-values are retained. Added uncertainty reporting does not establish increased experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical results. V2 supplies detailed benchmark results and new backbone, runtime, sensitivity, anomaly-type and hardness outcomes. For example, Table 20 reports IForest–Cardio AUC-PR of 0.718 with low-hardness synthesis versus 0.622 with original LLM-DAS. Some new reporting is inconsistent: PCA+LLM-DAS on Breastw has AUC-ROC 0.996 in Table 5 but 0.6196 in Table 7.

T1.justification: Section 6.14 adds Proposition 1 and its proof, transferring a synthetic-anomaly margin under Lipschitz continuity and epsilon-coverage assumptions. This is a limited conditional formalization of v1's intuitive boundary-refinement explanation, not a general guarantee for the complete framework. Section 6.16 also defines the Relative Hardness Ratio.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: LLMs act as algorithmists, generate reusable detector-specific synthesis code without accessing raw data, and improve anomaly detection across 36 benchmarks. Additional evidence and optional variants do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of local boundary refinement, detector-specific anomaly-type alignment and failures caused by overly hard synthetic anomalies. It qualifies the theory's applicability to non-smooth tree models and discusses lowering hardness to recover performance. Sections 6.14 and 6.19 also add stronger preservation and non-degradation assertions that exceed the conditional proof and conflict with reported failures.

D1.justification: The appendix supplies dataset properties, workflow pseudocode, complete example prompts, generated IForest synthesis code, and PyOD/DeepOD implementation information. The abstract adds a source-code repository link. These substantially improve documentation of the existing pipeline, although v1's explicit RTX 4090 hardware disclosure is removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds an isolation-method survey and references supporting already evaluated baselines and implementation libraries, including LOF, KNN, ICL, DTE and PyOD. The related-work narrative and positioning of the LLM as an algorithmist remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and most existing prose are preserved. Editorial changes include affiliations and conference headers, precise appendix cross-references, ethics and reproducibility statements, and a table of contents organizing the added appendix. Most expansion comes from added technical content rather than rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: V2 preserves the main figures and tables while adding Tables 3–22, Figures 6–13, workflow pseudocode, and prompt/code displays. These substantially expand visual presentation of detailed results and diagnostics. Figure 6 redisplays the existing Thyroid visualization alongside a new Vertebral analysis.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves an important documentation gap: v1 references an absent appendix, whereas v2 supplies prompts, example programs, dataset details and detailed results. Controlled anomaly-type tests, sensitivity checks and explicit failure analyses substantially improve assessment of the mechanism and its limits. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, including the Tables 5/7 inconsistency, undefined ± quantities and unsupported non-degradation assertions. The substantial improvement is in auditability and diagnostic evidence; headline performance remains essentially unchanged.
